content: 1. Omeprazole, amoxicillin, and clarithromycin are prescribed together to eradicate Helicobacter pylori and reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence. The recommended dosage is omeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1000 mg, and clarithromycin 500 mg, taken orally twice daily (morning and evening) for 10 days. No dose adjustment is necessary for renal impairment, but use should be avoided in hepatic impairment as safety and efficacy have not been established. 2. Co-administration of alfuzosin and clarithromycin is contraindicated as both drugs increase the QTc interval, posing a risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 3. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Clarithromycin and cisapride both prolong the QTc interval, making their co-administration contraindicated due to the risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. 5. Clarithromycin and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval, and their use together is contraindicated. 6. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as conivaptan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 8. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of dihydroergotamine (oral or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may result in vasospasm and ischemia of extremities and other tissues, including the central nervous system. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Dose adjustments are required for extensive metabolizers, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors is contraindicated. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates, ergonovine, and ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of vasospasm and ischemia. 12. Omeprazole decreases the levels of erlotinib by altering gastric pH, reducing its solubility and bioavailability. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of finerenone and flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope with flibanserin. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Clarithromycin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval, making their co-administration contraindicated. 16. Clarithromycin and indapamide both increase the QTc interval, and their use together is contraindicated. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QTc prolongation. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lomitapide and lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe toxicity. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 20. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse reactions. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Omeprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir by inhibiting its conversion to the active M8 metabolite and reducing its absorption due to increased gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Clarithromycin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval, making their co-administration contraindicated. 27. Clarithromycin and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval, and clarithromycin increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation. 28. Quinidine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval, making their co-administration contraindicated. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels of rifabutin by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Omeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, leading to treatment failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of rhabdomyolysis. 32. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Omeprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, while clarithromycin increases its levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Clarithromycin and adagrasib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. Co-administration should be avoided or closely monitored. 36. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole and clarithromycin by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the exposure and toxicity of its cytotoxic component, DM1. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of afatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of almotriptan, alprazolam, and amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 40. Clarithromycin and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval, making their co-administration contraindicated. 41. Clarithromycin and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or closely monitored with ECG. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 43. Clarithromycin and amoxapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 44. Clarithromycin and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 45. Clarithromycin increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by decreasing their metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 46. Apomorphine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 48. Clarithromycin increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 49. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 50. Arsenic trioxide and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 51. Artemether and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 52. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 53. Clarithromycin and asenapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 54. Omeprazole decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility and plasma concentrations. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 55. Atomoxetine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 56. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administered, the atorvastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 57. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
